messages:
alex: heads up — seeing a spike in GPU provisioning failures in eu-west1. lots of pods stuck Pending with volume attach errors. noticed node gnode-472 has /scratch nvme read queue depth pegged.

sara: saw that too, spotted a short network flap ~1729004200 that coincided with kubelet restarting on a handful of nodes. after kubelet restart the scratch cleaner restarted and immediately started a deep scrub. read queue depth jumped to 512 and stayed there. :grimacing:

lee: paste from the node: 
```
iostat -x /dev/nvme0n1 1 3
Device:         rrqm/s wrqm/s   r/s   w/s  rsec/s  wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.00  0.00  25.00   0.00 2048.00   0.00   81.92   11.43 120.4 120.2   0.0   80.0  99.9
```
That avgqu-sz=11.43 and %util almost 100%.

matt_ops: provisioning path times out when attach waits on reads — controller logs show "attach timed out waiting for device ready". suspect heavy scrub + kubelet restart + small network hiccup = wedged read queues.

oncall-sre: started incident INC-2024-5123 and notified oncall rotation. plan: cordon + drain two most affected nodes, restart scratch-cleaner on remaining pool, reduce scrub concurrency global flag.

sara: quick mitigation idea — reduce scrub/concurrency and pause fstrim for the pool for 10 minutes, then probe. scrub sampler config is in ops-config map `scratch-cleaner` under `concurrency` and `max-reads`.

alex: doing canary rollback of scrub sampler on eu-west1-small ring now: setting `concurrency: 2` `max-reads: 64` via `kubectl -n infra patch cm scratch-cleaner -p '...'.` will monitor attach success rate.

lee: FYI the kernel dmesg showed repeated: "blk_fill_rwbs: queue depth exceeded, queuing scatter-gather" and timestamps aligned with the scrub restart. probably too many asynchronous reads queued when network/IO bus briefly paused.

matt_ops: if rollback doesn't help we should consider draining and rebooting gnode-472/473 — reboot clears NVMe controller internal queue and resets firmware state. risk: longer disruption for pods, but faster than waiting for scrub finish.

oncall-sre: agreed. plan staged: 1) patch scrub sampler (in flight) 2) monitor 5m 3) if no improvement, cordon+drain gnode-472 then reboot 4) alert customers if rollout >30m.

sara: after patch attach success rate improved on canary (3/5 pods that were pending moved to Bound within ~40s). looks promising. :thumbsup:

alex: leaving scrub concurrency lowered for 30m across eu-west1. scheduling follow-up to audit scrub start triggers — we shouldn't restart deep-scrubs on kubelet restart during high-provisioning windows.

lee: adding kernel-side mitigation ticket — investigate handling of NVMe controller pause during driver reset and possible firmware backpressure signals. might need vendor input.

matt_ops: capture: `nvme list && nvme get-feature /dev/nvme0n1 -f 0x7` and nvme-fw logs pre/post for vendors.

sre-bot: incident INC-2024-5123 created by oncall-sre. severity: P2. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2024-5123

oncall-sre: closing loop — current status: canary OK, rolling change to other nodes in eu-west1 during low-traffic window. postmortem skeleton assigned to @sara.

alex: notes for postmortem — consider: scrub restart policy on kubelet restart, fstrim schedule alignment with GPU provisioning windows, and adding a read-queue monitor to alert before attach failures.

sara: thanks team. will write postmortem and vendor outreach if kernel/firmware indicates controller-side throttling.
